reading: The track series is the owner-lens favourite of the whole tournament (feedback 8.4-9.1 in every round since Signal Box) and wins soul wherever its light stays on live things (the now lamp, the lit run, the tubes). What sank it in the main rounds was never the idea: lines drawn where there is no order (git graph, subway map), slate and steel so quiet that the pages read green-and-grey, tiny usability slips (a 5px 'here' dot, an icon-only bar, late shown by colour alone, a bare pencil), and near-duplicate children. In tour round 1 both carried designs tied at 7.84 (+0.19 on Desk Terminal, Joined). Branch Lines won 7 top fours and 8 promise votes, the most in heat a, because four boxed pages started drawing their own data: the line from home on Ideas, the indication shelf with '6 working · 7 off', the double-track chat, and a figure in every head. Signal Box Relaid won feedback (8.9) and type (8.5) by putting the owner's favourite element back on every page: the ring-drop-chamfer head bracket, T buffers with the way on beside them, one lamp legend, setup as a vertical station line, and the big condensed lit question. What holds them back now: (1) Home. Style, system, skeptic and soul all said it is still the parent's, and the skeptic said all six track entrants share one Home. (2) Colour. Chat and Status are 97-99% green-and-grey. (3) Devices that make the family decode: bare station numbers colliding at 18-21 min, and shelf lamps with no names. (4) The backlit steel 'here' slab, which looks disabled. (5) Wrong counts ('Plans 1' over three plans) and a week rail under one row only. (6) Relaid's stretched Status boards (150px of dead slate), its tall radar, and a title that lights the motif ('line') instead of the job. (7) The row afterglow, which is still invisible as a steel wash. To win, each line must: change Home at page scale with a drawing of Home's own data; give grounded colour a job in solids (the kind rings in terracotta, moss and wheat, and the family's own material); name everything an instrument shows and count only what is shown; keep the light on the short live list at full strength (the key word at 40px with the two-layer halo, the lit run, the box's resting glow, tubes at 1.0, lamps with hot cores, and an afterglow edge that shows at 120ms); and finish the usability floor (44px targets, sentence-case controls, late in words, 'Edit' in words, a latched dark 'here'). On titles, 'What's the plan?' is the judged best and the lineage's to keep. 'What shall we plan?' is the judges' own fix for Relaid. The motif word and 'next' have both failed.

briefs.name: Branch Lines, Trued
briefs.hypothesis: Branch Lines tied first with the most promise votes because its pages draw their own data. Every fault its judges named is a finishing fault: stations that must be decoded, lamps with no names, wrong counts, the backlit slab, the busy chat, too little colour, and a Home that looks like its parent. Most of those fixes are themselves new drawings: named stations lit from their rows, one lit instrument with labelled banks, rails on every week of the month, a calmer two-track chat with only the newest stop lit, and a form that shows what is still needed. Fixing each in the design's own language should lift it clear of 7.84 and of Joined, and keep it distinct from Relaid, whose identity is brackets and buffers rather than drawings of data.
briefs.brief:
Start from t1-track-graft's files (css built by src/build.py from track.css, phosphor.css, relight.css and branch.css; the templates). Keep every branch drawing and finish each one. 1. THE QUESTION AND THE LIGHT (Home). In _ask.html:

. Set it as Home's largest head: Archivo 700, font-stretch 80%, 2.5rem/1 (clamp(1.9rem, 7vw, 2.5rem) on the phone), letter-spacing -0.012em, colour --heading #ebe6da. Light 'plan' in #6dff9c with E1's two layers (0 0 .45em rgb(109 255 156/.45), 0 0 1.3em rgb(109 255 156/.22)). Section h2s stay at 1.42rem, so the squint reads question, then tube, then heads. The box keeps E4's resting glow (0 0 38px -20px brand/.6, edge 30% brand). Send keeps E3's ring and pool. The greeting keeps E7's pool from below at 0.13 with its scanlines. The tube stays at screenGlow 1.0 in the 3px graphite case. 2. 'HERE' ON EVERY PAGE. Delete the backlit steel key (radial #879dae to #748a9b with dark ink) from the bar, the Ideas tabs, To do's Open key, Plans' List/Month, the settings nav and today on the month. Draw T1-32 in its place: a latched cell #26313a with ink #ebe6da and inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255/.05), a 2px steel cap on the edge that meets the line (the bar's foot, riding its 1px #2e343b rule; the top on the phone's tab bar; the left in the settings nav), and Branch Lines' small ring lamp on the rule under the bar key. Latched filter keys take the same drawing. 3. COLOUR WITH JOBS. Give the steel companion a breath more chroma: --accent/--steel #a7c4d8 becomes #9cc3dd, for links, the family's bar, their initial rings and the latched cap. Kind colour lives in the ring alone, in Relaid's grounded hues: restaurant terracotta #df987c (off amber, so amber means late alone), outing moss #b5c87d (off the second green #86d9a6), seasonal wheat #c3a85d. Kind words stay ink-2. Chat's family plates become #1b2531 (a step bluer than #1c252b) with the 3px steel bar. Plans cyan #70dcf4 marks every plan stop (the fortnight, the month, the Plans list). Status lamps get one meaning each (8). 4. AN AFTERGLOW THAT SHOWS. Replace the 12% steel wash with a lit edge: box-shadow inset 2px 0 0 #86d9a6, 0 0 18px -10px #86d9a6, over a 6% steel wash. It comes on in .12s and fades over var(--afterglow) 1.2s, on :hover and :focus-within of .idea-card/.idea-row, To do rows, timetable rows, Settings rows and Status rows, so it still shows at 120ms after the pointer leaves. On Ideas, the same pointing lights the row's station (7): the afterglow's second place. 5. HOME. - Setup. Keep Branch Lines' own horizontal line of three stops, on slate #0f1519 with the 1px amber edge only. Every stop is a hollow amber ring numbered 1 to 3 in 13px DM Mono. The current step's ring takes a phosphor rim with E21's tight halo and the words 'Next step' in 13px sage above it; done steps (on a real install) are a filled sage lamp with a tick. Set each step with a run-in bold action (T1-05): the action in 600 ink, then ', so …' in 400 ink-2, at the 16px body with balanced wrap. The rail ends at a T buffer (a 14×2 bar on a 2×10 upright, #8a9aa8) beside 'All the setup steps'. - Coming up. The head carries its figure: '4', with 'more / after Next up' stacked beside it on the numeral's baseline at 13px. Keep the fortnight: the NOW lamp breathing (the page's only breathing lamp), the lit run with a hot core to the first stop (L229), cyan stop rings, and Archivo 300 day numerals with month and weekday stacked in 13px mono. Set plate titles at 15px/600 so 'Mount St. Helens day trip' holds one line. The rail ends at a T buffer 16px past the last stop, with 'All plans' beside it and no overrun. - To do. The head figure '4 open / 2 late' makes '2 late' an amber link to the To do page's first late row, which lands with E10's 1.8s flash. Keep the 'Due' legend, the 8.5rem margin and nowrap stamps. Carry the lit run down the rail from the now tick to the next due stop, and end the rail at a T buffer beside 'All 4'. - The kids' wishes lose their tray. They become one 44px line at the foot of the To do column: gift ring, 'The kids' wishes', 'Maya 0 open · Theo 0 open' (names link to their lists; a kid's top wish follows the name when there is one), and 'All' at the right. The To do and Lately added columns end within a row of each other. - Lately added is kept as it is, with 'Something to eat · 2 restaurants to try' as its last row in terracotta. 6. CHAT. - The page head is drawn as on every other page: ring, 'Vera' flush left, the lede under it. It is no longer set right against the spine. - Keep the double-track main line and calm it. The rails are 2px, 18px apart. The family's stop is a 12px steel ring with no initial; their name ('Sam') moves into the plate's head in #9cc3dd. Her stop is her 22px glyph screen. Each time is printed once across the rails on a #0b0e0c patch in 13px DM Mono. Keep the 'Sun 27 Sep' day tie. - Light only the newest stop (T1-35): her newest screen with E19's halo, and its time in #86d9a6 with a soft halo. Older plates go matte (#111712, 1px #2e3a33 edge, no bloom). The rails still merge through one 45° pair into a lit run that ends in the ring on the composer, labelled 'your turn' in 13px sage. The composer takes Home's E4 resting glow. - On the phone it folds to one rail, as now. 7. IDEAS: THE LINE FROM HOME, FINISHED. - A tube about 7.5rem tall across the column. One VT323 line across its top: 'THE LINE FROM HOME · 10 PLACES · MINUTES BY ROAD'. - The axis starts at the 15-minute milepost. 'home' is lit at the left, joined to 15 by a short stub with one 45° jog (the railway's not-to-scale mark, replacing the '/ /' breaks). The lit run goes only from home to the nearest station. - Every place is a tick on the rail. Only the nearest, the furthest and the pointed-at station carry words on the glass, name and time together: 'Pumpkin patch 18 min' under the rail, 'Cannon Beach 2 h 45' over it. No bare numbers anywhere. - Each named station is a link to its row (#idea-N) with a 44px hit area. Pointing at or focusing any row lights its station (hot core and two-layer halo, on in .12s, out over 1.2s) and shows its name over the rail. build.py writes the :has() rule for every row position up to 40, not 16. - Head: 'Ideas 12', with 'ideas / 10 on the line' stacked on the numeral's baseline at 13px. 'Save a thought' (secondary) and 'Add an idea' (the one green key) sit on the title's baseline. - One control per filter. All ideas and Restaurants stay as the two page tabs (the latched cell marks here). The Kind select drops 'restaurant'. Search, Kind, Status, For and Filter sit on one slate strip. - Table columns: # right-aligned; Idea (ring, name, kind word in ink-2); For; Drive in bold figures with light units and padded minutes ('2 h 05 min'); Way (the compass) in its own column. Column heads are 13px sentence case. 8. STATUS: ONE LIT INSTRUMENT. - The spend tube and the indication shelf go behind one thin graphite case (3px bezel, hairline lip, vent chin, power lamp) with two windows: the glass, with the spend at E12-E15 full light, and a recessed well #080c0d holding the lamps. No slate box floats beside it and nothing is stretched. - Every lamp gets its name under it in 12-13px ink-2: Chat, Digest, Lookups, Fallback | Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, Telegram | Calendar, Weather, Web, Digest, This page. Each bank has a caption with its count on one baseline: 'Who answers 3 of 4', 'Keys 1 of 4', 'Connected 2 of 5'. Each lamp is a link to its row. - One meaning per signal, split so 'off' stops alarming. Working is a lit lamp (white-hot core, two halos, steady; only a NOW lamp breathes anywhere). Waiting is a 7px steel dot (the digest not yet sent). Off by choice is a pewter ring (reading the web, the fallback). Not set up is a dashed pewter ring (L133): the three missing keys and the calendar. Needs a look is an amber half lamp. Red is only for something that has stopped. - The tally sits on the case's chin baseline: '6 working · 1 waiting · 2 off · 4 not set up', figures in 40px Archivo 600 at wdth 75, each followed by the lamp it counts. 'Change the limit' goes in the chin caption. The lamp legend (T1-26) is printed once under the case. - Below it, Who answers is the lit line lamp to lamp, ending in one 45° turnout to a T buffer for 'If that one cannot'. Keys and Connected to are one-line rows under heads that carry their counts. Every board is as tall as its rows. 9. PLANS. - The head counts what is coming: 'Plans 5', with 'coming / next tomorrow 10:00' stacked beside it. List and Month are latched keys in the head. 'Put something on the calendar' stays on the title's baseline. - Month: week tracks on every week row, not only the last. Each week's 2px rail is its foot. Past weeks' rails are dimmed to #2e343b with pewter rings. Each plan is a cyan ring at its hour. Today's NOW lamp carries its lit run to the next plan. Today's date is the latched cell with its steel cap. Weekend columns stay a step lighter. - List: the timetable as now (NOW lamp, lit run, day and hour in the margin, cyan rings, 'Move it' and 'Cancel it'). 10. TO DO PAGE. - Head: 'Things to do 4', with 'open / 2 late' stacked. The orphan 'Show' label is dropped. Open, Done, Cancelled and All are latched keys, followed by the search field and its key. - Each row: a square tick well with a 44px hit area, the title, Who, Due in words (amber 'was due 3 days ago'), and an 'Edit' key with pencil and word. - The rail on the left: amber late lamps; the NOW tick drawn as a 2px lit rule across the gap between the last late row and the first one to come; the lit run down to the next due stop; hollow steel rings after it; and a dashed ring for a task with no date. Where a reminder is set, the Due cell shows a bell and its time. 11. SETTINGS AND THE FORM. - Settings keeps its lamp list (T1-24), now with the signals of section 8. The section pages' side nav uses the same rows, with the latched cell and its cap on the left. - The New idea form hangs its labels right-aligned in an 8.5rem margin (the timetable's margin) at 13px, with the fields on the line. The two required fields (Title, Kind) each carry a hollow amber lamp in the margin that fills sage once the field is valid (.field:has(:required:valid) .req-lamp), so the form shows what is still needed, as its lede says. 'Add it' is the one green key, with E3. 12. EVERYWHERE. Nothing under 12-13px (the stacked head units were 11.52px). 0 targets under 44px on desktop and phone. Reduced motion, more contrast (no halos, no scanlines, no afterglow) and forced colours are kept. Every form keeps its csrf and once tokens. No inline style: SVG geometry goes in presentation attributes, as the graft did. The sheet is at 57.2K of 60K, so pay for this by deleting what it replaces (the backlit key, the shelf's own box, the kids' tray and the rules for the old initials) and let build.py squeeze the rest.
briefs.borrows:
The judges' fixes, most-cited first:
(1) Home still reads as the parent's (style, system, skeptic, soul). Answered by: the 40px question with 'plan' lit (system, soul, style: 'take the revival's 40px greeting'); the kids' wishes folded into one line (system, style; on Trued also feedback and skeptic); the setup stops hollow amber with the current one lit and labelled 'Next step' (style #4; usability on Trued); T buffers at every line end with the way on (style #5).
(2) 90% green share, with Chat and Status monochrome (feedback, style, system, skeptic). Answered by: steel at #9cc3dd, the kind rings in terracotta, moss and wheat (system, skeptic), the family's plates and initials in steel (feedback), and one meaning per lamp.
(3) The line from home collides and must be decoded (usability, interaction, type #4, system, style #2, skeptic #3, soul #5). Answered by: only the nearest, furthest and pointed-at stations named in words; the axis starting at 15 min behind one 45° jog; the lit run only to the nearest station; 'minutes by road' on the glass; every row lighting its station, with rules to 40 rows (usability).
(4) Status shelf lamps have no names, and '7 off' alarms (interaction, usability, skeptic #2). Answered by: a name under every lamp, bank captions with counts, and off split from not set up. Soul #2 asked for the tube and shelf in one bezel; system asked to fold 'Change the limit' into the caption and set the counts on the shelf's baseline.
(5) The backlit 'here' slab reads as disabled (system, skeptic #1). Answered by T1-32 from Trued (tour/t1-a/variants/t1-track-refine/src/trued.css lines 101-108 and 150-165).
(6) Plans says '1 plan in September' over three plans, and its week rail sits under the last row only (feedback, system, usability, skeptic #4, style #6, interaction). Answered by counting what is coming and railing every week.
(7) Chat: the double rail reads busy (feedback); the title is set backwards (type #5, interaction); soul #4 asked to light only the newest stop (T1-35 from Night Departures).
(8) Row afterglow is invisible (soul #3). Answered by T1-33's sage edge, visible at 120ms.
(9) Type: the stacked unit on the numeral's baseline at 13px (type #1); padded minutes (#2); direction in its own column (#3); the orphan 'Show' dropped (#6); the smallest text raised to 12-13px (usability).
(10) From Trued's judges, still true here: a lit rule at NOW in To do (interaction) and a bell in the Due cell for a reminder (usability).
Small borrows answering faults: T buffers and 'your turn' from the lineage's own Relaid (tour/t2-a/variants/t1-track-revival/src/relaid.css, .buffer); run-in bold setup actions T1-05 (tour/t1-b/variants/t1-figure-refine/templates/home.html lines 140-158); and L133, the dashed outline for 'not now' (Attract Mode, rounds/r8/palettes/r8-rand-3.json), used only for 'not set up' and 'no date'.
briefs.avoids: Home looking like the parent (40px lit question, lit 'Next step', kids in one line, buffers). The 90% green-and-grey page (steel chroma, grounded kind rings, cyan plan stops, lamps with one meaning). 'A lookup puzzle' and colliding 7-6-8 numbers on the line from home. Unlabelled shelf lamps, the '7 off' alarm and dead slate beside the tube. The backlit steel slab. 'Plans 1' over three plans, and a week rail under one row. The busy double rail and the backwards Chat title. All her bubbles lit alike. The invisible steel-wash afterglow. Amber on Restaurant. 11.5px stacked units. The orphan 'Show'. 'What's next for us?', whose 'next' leaves out ideas and wishes and repeats NEXT UP. Also the git-graph fault: no new rail is added where there is no order.
briefs.title: What’s the *plan*? This is the lineage's best-judged title: first or joint first in 13 of 16 notes in tour round 1, and the system lens gave it to the track series by name. It is the family's own kitchen-table question and holds one line at 40px on a phone. Its lit word is the planner's whole job, since weekends, outings, the calendar, reminders and ideas are all 'the plan'. Its echo of the placeholder's 'Plans for the weekend' reads as a question followed by its answers. It replaces the design's 'What's next for us?', whose 'next' narrows the job and doubles the NEXT UP on the tube beside it.

briefs.name: Relaid, Finished
briefs.hypothesis: Signal Box Relaid won feedback (8.9) and type (8.5) with the owner's favourite element on every page. It lost points on a few things only: a title that lights the motif, a stretched Status with dead slate, a tall radar, 13px Home rows, a bare pencil and some tracked caps. Fixing those in its own grammar should lift it above 8 while it stays the lineage's second, distinct line: chamfers, buffers and a legend rather than drawings of each page's data. That grammar means the head's figure standing at the T buffer, the legend doubling as Status's tally, and the form drawn as a line. So it does not take Branch Lines' line from home, shelf or title figures, which some lenses asked for, because that would merge the two lines.
briefs.brief:
Start from t1-track-revival's files (src/relaid.css squeezed by build.py; the templates). Keep its grammar whole: straight runs, one 45° chamfer at each turn, terminus rings, T buffers with the way on beside them, the head bracket (ring, 1px wire, one chamfer, a shelf the keys stand on), one lamp legend, the latched 'here' cell (#26313a, a 3px steel run and a ring lamp on the bar's line), kind colour in the ring alone (terracotta, moss, wheat), and the lit list at full strength (E1-E4, E7 at 0.13, E12-E17 at screenGlow 1.0 on thin graphite cases, E19, E20 with white-hot cores). 1. THE TITLE. In _ask.html:

. Keep Relaid's setting: 40px Archivo 700 condensed (28px on the phone), heading #ebe6da, with 'plan' in E1's two layers. The glow moves from the motif to the job; the 'we' and the size stay. 2. HOME. - The greeting's sight line (interaction: the tube competes with the question). Keep the tube's glass at 1.0 but cut its room spill (E12's 0 0 80px -36px from 45% to 25% phosphor) and the case's outer halo. The box keeps E4's resting glow and Send keeps E3's ring and pool, so the question, the box and Send are the brightest group in a squint. - 'WEDNESDAY 30 SEPTEMBER' in tracked mono caps becomes 'Wednesday 30 September' in Archivo 500 at 15px, no caps, no tracking. On the tube, 'Thursday 1 October, 10:00' is joined with a no-break space so the time never breaks from its date. - Setup. Keep the vertical station line (amber terminus, one 44px row per step, the buffer beside 'All the setup steps'). The first stop no longer glows green, which reads as done. The current step is a hollow ring with a phosphor rim, E21's tight halo and 'Next step' in 13px beside it. The rest are hollow amber rings; done steps are filled sage with a tick. - Coming up. The rail stops at a T buffer 16px after the last stop, with 'All plans' beside it: hang each plate from its stop's left edge so the last plate ends before the buffer. Each plate takes a 2px plans-cyan cap (#70dcf4 at 70%) and the to-come rings stay cyan, so the plans carry one cool period colour and the board is not grey-green alone. - Row size. To do, Coming up and Lately added titles go up to the 16px body step at 600, from about 13px. 13px stays for labels, stamps and legends. - To do on Home: '2 late' stands at the head's buffer as an amber link. The lit run is carried down the rail from the now tick to the next due stop. - The kids' wishes become one 44px line under both columns: gift ring, 'The kids' wishes', 'Maya 0 open · Theo 0 open', and 'All' at the right. 3. THE HEAD'S FIGURE STANDS AT THE BUFFER. The bracket's shelf runs to a T buffer at the head's right edge, and the page's count stands beside the buffer: numeral at 24px Archivo 600 in bone, unit at 13px ink-2. Ideas: '12 ideas'. To do: '4 open · 2 late', with '2 late' in amber linking to the first late row, which lands with E10's flash. Plans: '5 coming', counting what is coming. The figure belongs to the line, not to the title; that is the difference from Branch Lines' stacked title figures. Heads with no keys (Status, Settings) still draw no line. 4. IDEAS. - 'Save a thought for later ⌄' leaves the tab row and joins the head as a secondary key beside 'Add an idea'. The bracket's shelf then holds only the All ideas | Restaurants keys. - Cap the radar tube at the height of the first eight rows (about 22rem) and make it sticky under the bar (top: calc(bar height + 1rem)), so it stops being the tallest, brightest block. Keep its reading lines ('Nearest #7 Pumpkin patch at Bi-Mart farm 18 min NW', 'Furthest #4 …') and the caption under the case. - Column heads 'Drive', 'Way', 'For' and '#' in sentence case, 13px label steel, no tracking. Keep the table standard: # right-aligned, the kind as an ink word in its own column, Drive and Way apart, figures tabular. - Give the lede 8px more room above the bracket's keys. 5. STATUS. - Fill the dead band beside the tube. The lamp legend moves up under the lede, beside the tube, and becomes the tally: every signal with its count, in DM Sans 15px with tabular figures: 'live 6 · waiting 1 · off 2 · not set up 4 · needs a look 0', each word after its lamp. 'Not set up' is a dashed pewter ring (L133), so the three missing keys and the calendar stop reading as off. The lede keeps 'Today: about $0.00 of the $2.00 daily limit. Change the limit'. - Every board is as tall as its content (.monitors{align-items:start}), so Keys ends at its last row and the 150px of empty slate is gone. Who answers keeps its lit line and the fallback siding with its buffer. 6. PLANS. The bracket holds List | Month only. Earlier and Later move onto the month's own head row, beside 'September 2026' at 24px. The head's figure '5 coming' stands at its buffer. Today's date is the latched cell with the steel cap. Plan chips carry their cyan ring, and past days sit a step darker. 7. TO DO PAGE. The pencil gets the word: a 44px 'Edit' key with pencil and word. Keep the latched Open/Done/Cancelled/All keys and the search on the shelf, the lit NOW tick and run, amber stamps, and deadlines in words. 8. CHAT. - One timetable rule for the app: every time goes in the left margin, right-aligned, tabular, 13px DM Mono, the family's too, where they used to sit at the wire's end. - The family's plates keep the right side, so mine and hers still read apart, joined to their stop by the 1px steel wire. - The composer takes Home's resting glow (E4: 0 0 38px -20px brand/.6, edge 30% brand), so the lit 'your turn' ring and the box read as one lit stop. 9. THE FORM AS A LINE (New idea, in Relaid's grammar). A terminus ring stands beside 'Title', and a 2px steel rail runs down the form's left gutter with a hollow stop at each field's label. A stop lights phosphor while its field has focus (L100's coupling: .field:focus-within .stop, on in .12s, off over 1.2s). The rail ends at a T buffer beside 'Add it', the one green key. Sign in keeps its line; Settings keeps its lamped list. 10. EVERYWHERE. - Row afterglow: a 2px sage edge (inset 2px 0 0 #86d9a6, 0 0 18px -10px #86d9a6) over a 6% steel wash, on in .12s, off over 1.2s, so it still shows at 120ms. - Find and fix the one small target on every page (probably the skip link or the wordmark's link box) and make it 44px. - 0 targets under 44px. Nothing under 13px. - Reduced motion, more contrast and forced colours are kept, and forms keep their tokens. - The sheet is at 56.4K of 60K: pay for this by deleting the 13px row overrides, the old legend's position and the tracked-caps rules.
briefs.borrows:
Relaid's own judges' fixes, most-cited first:
(1) The title lights the motif, not the job (all eight lenses). Answered by 'What shall we plan?' at the same size: feedback's own fix, listed in the lessons' TRY NEXT; type asked to light the job word.
(2) Status: Keys and Connected to stretched, leaving about 150px of empty slate (feedback, soul, style, system, interaction, skeptic). Answered by boards sized to content. The dead band beside the tube (feedback, system) is filled with Relaid's own legend turned into the tally.
(3) Ideas: the tall portrait radar (soul: cap it to the first eight rows; system: a short strip). Answered by the cap plus sticky; the line from home is declined here to keep the two lines apart. 'Save a thought' looks like a third tab (usability, interaction): moved to the head.
(4) To do's bare pencil (interaction, usability): 'Edit' in words. '2 late' in Home's To do head (interaction).
(5) Type: Home rows at 13px raised to the body step (#1); the tracked-caps date kicker (#2); the tube's date/time break (#3); Chat's times into the same margin as To do's (#4); lede spacing (#5); tracked column heads (#6).
(6) Soul: the chat box matte at rest while its lamp is lit, so it takes Home's resting glow. Row afterglow invisible (from the graft's soul notes, true here too), so a sage edge.
(7) Plans: the bracket crams the view keys and Earlier/Later (system), so the month keys get their own row.
(8) Interaction: the Next up tube's bloom competes with the question, so the tube's spill is cut while the glass stays at 1.0. Fix the one small target on every page.
(9) Feedback: the grey-heavy colour gets a cyan cap on the plans and cyan to-come rings. A head figure beside Ideas, To do and Plans is set at the buffer, in Relaid's grammar.
(10) Feedback and own weakness: the fortnight's rail should end at its last stop's buffer.
(11) Usability on Trued, which applies here: a green first setup lamp reads as done.
Small borrows answering those faults: L133, the dashed outline for 'not now' (Attract Mode, rounds/r8/palettes/r8-rand-3.json, 'table.month td.outside{border:1px dashed …}'), only for 'not set up'; and L100's coupling of light and focus (Night Timetable, rounds/r10/variants/r10-wild-3/sheet.css line 1368, .welcome .ask:focus-within::before), taken only as a stop that lights while its field has focus, for the form.
briefs.avoids: 'What shall we line up?' as a pun on the motif. The 150px of dead slate under Keys and the dead band beside the spend tube. The tall, brightest radar. 'Save a thought' dressed as a third tab. The bare pencil. 13px Home rows. 'WEDNESDAY 30 SEPTEMBER' in tracked caps, and the same for the column heads. The date and time breaking on the tube. The family's times at the far end of long wires. A matte chat box under a lit terminus. The fortnight's rail running a plate's width past its last stop. A green first setup lamp that reads as done. The one small target per page. The tube outshining the question. A page of grey and green alone. Merging into Branch Lines: no line from home, no shelf, no stacked title figures.
briefs.title: What shall we *plan*? This title is untried. It is the fix the feedback lens wrote for this very design, and the tour's lessons list it under TRY NEXT for the track series. It keeps Relaid's household 'we' and its 40px condensed setting, which soul and interaction called the best-lit and most visible question in the heat. It moves the glow from the motif ('line') to the job ('plan'), so it no longer reads as a pun and no longer splits 'line up'. It is an invitation to decide together and tell Vera, and it fits one line on a phone at 28px. Its one risk is the formality of 'shall', which is what this round will test.

briefs.name: Branch Lines, Lit Sill
briefs.hypothesis: Branch Lines' boxed pages won when they started drawing their own data. Home, the page the family sees first, stayed the parent's; the colour stayed green-and-grey; and Status's lamps said nothing by name. Four features rebuilt in its own steel-on-slate line target exactly those. The greeting stands on the Coming up line, with the tube as the first station and the airglow rising off the lit run (L099 and L098, gems). The family's hand becomes ink (L004, gem). The lamps are typed on Status's glass as named strings (L253). The line is set on opening like a route (L110, gem). Home should then read new at a glance above the fold, Chat and Home should gain a grounded solid with a job, and the tube's light should return onto live data.
briefs.brief:
Start from t1-track-graft's files. Keep every branch drawing: the line from home, the double-track chat, the head figures, the Plans timetable and the Settings lamp list. Graft four features, each rebuilt in steel on slate with lamps, and apply the lineage's key fixes (E).

A. THE GREETING STANDS ON THE COMING UP LINE (Home; L099 and L098, gems).
- Recompose section.welcome at 64rem and wider as [Next up tube | question and box]: grid-template-columns 25rem 1fr, with the tube placed left by grid-area. The box stays first in the DOM, so Tab reaches the box before the tube's link. The tube is portrait (radar over the Next up words) in the 3px graphite case at screenGlow 1.0, and keeps its classes (.crt.next-up), so the harness's motion-on frames still find it.
- The board's foot is the line, as a sill. A 2px steel rail (#58697a) runs the greeting's full width along its bottom edge. At its left end is the NOW lamp: breathing (the page's only breathing lamp), with 'now' at 13px in sage.
- From the tube's chin power lamp, a 2px lit wire drops to the rail. Station one is Next up: the tube is the first stop. The run from NOW to station one is lit with a hot core (L229), and the sill's own border is at 38% brand along that run.
- Stations two to five (Sun 4, Fri 9, Sat 17, Sat 24 Oct) are cyan rings across the rail under the question column. Their day numerals (Archivo 300 30px, month and weekday stacked in 13px mono) stand above the rail inside the glass. Their plates hang below the sill, outside the board, on 1px drops. The rail ends in a T buffer at the right with 'All plans'. Draw the geometry as SVG presentation attributes in home.html.
- The light. The airglow rises off the lit run: .welcome::before, 9rem tall from the sill, linear-gradient(to top, rgb(109 255 156/.12), transparent), masked by radial-gradient(40% 100% at 18% 100%, #000, transparent 85%). It is brightest over the lit run and gone before the question. E7's pool from the lower left stays at 0.13 and is now explained by it. The sill spills softly onto the plates below (box-shadow 0 24px 40px -30px rgb(109 255 156/.35), L099). The cobalt corner stays off. Under more contrast, drop the airglow and the spill.
- Under the lit run, below the sill and left of the plates: the 'Coming up' head with its figure '4', 'more / after Next up' stacked on the numeral's baseline at 13px, and the source note 'Google Calendar is not connected, so these are the plans the bot made.' The separate Coming up tray is gone.
- Next comes setup (see E), then the desk: To do's timetable | Lately added, with the kids' wishes as one 44px line at the foot of To do ('The kids' wishes · Maya 0 open · Theo 0 open · All').
- Phone: the box, the ways to start, then the tube. The line turns vertical down the left gutter from the tube's chin: the NOW lamp, the lit run to station one at the chin, the four plans as rows beside the rail (the day in the margin), then a T buffer and 'All plans'. The airglow rises at the chin.

B. THE FAMILY'S HAND IS INK (L004, gem, in Late Set's praised midnight form).
- Tokens: --ink-plate #182536, --ink-edge #2e4460, --ink-bar #86a9cc, --ink-well #0d141c, --ink-well-edge #34485e. Keep chroma at .035 or less and clear of Tokyo Night's #7aa2f7.
- One rule: the machine's words and marks are phosphor, the board and rails are slate and steel, and what the family wrote is ink.
- Chat: the family's plates are filled #182536 with a 1px #2e4460 edge and the 3px #86a9cc bar, and their stop rings are filled ink. Vera's plates stay green-black glass #111712.
- Plans: Coming up's plates under the sill, the Plans list's plan plates and the month's event chips become ink plates with a 2px #86a9cc cap along the top (plans the family put on the calendar). The cyan rings stay.
- Fields: every field the family types in (inputs, selects, textareas, both searches, the New idea form, the Settings forms, To do's tick wells) is an ink well #0d141c with a #34485e edge; caret and focus stay phosphor (E4). Home's box stays on the greeting's glass (L004's caveat).
- Never use ink on boards, trays, rows or cards (navy card surfaces failed in round 13), and never as a text colour. Names stay ink or ink-2 and links stay steel and underlined, so blue text always means a link.

C. STATUS: THE LAMPS TYPED ON THE GLASS (L253).
- Delete the separate indication shelf and its well. The spend tube becomes the one instrument, about 30rem × 19rem (near 4:3) in the thin case.
- On the glass, in VT323: 'SPENT TODAY, ABOUT', '$0.00', '[....................] 0%', 'OF THE $2.00 DAILY LIMIT', a dim rule, then three lamp strings. Each string is an <a> row 44px tall linking to its board (#answers, #keys, #connected):
  'WHO ANSWERS ● ● ● ○ 3 OF 4'
  'KEYS ◌ ● ◌ ◌ 1 OF 4'
  'CONNECTED ◌ ● ○ · ● 2 OF 5'
- The lamps are spans drawn in the tube's strengths: working is a hot core #a9ffc7 in a blip halo, waiting a dim dot, off a dim ring, not set up a dim dashed ring. E15 inverse shows on hover and focus. Each link's words read out in full ('Who answers: 3 of 4 working').
- Beside the instrument, with no dead slate: the tally in words and 40px Archivo figures, '6 working · 1 waiting · 2 off · 4 not set up'; the lamp legend in the page's colours (lit lamp, steel dot, pewter ring, dashed pewter ring, amber half, red stopped); and 'Change the limit' as the tube's caption under the case.
- The boards below carry their counts in their heads ('Who answers 3 of 4') and their page lamps. Who answers stays lit lamp to lamp, with the fallback's 45° turnout to a buffer.

D. THE ROUTE SETS ON OPENING (L110, gem; soul's 'travelling afterglow wake').
- Once per load, each tube's roll bar sweeps its glass: Attract Mode's scan, a 2px white-hot line with a 14px bloom, 1.25s after a .15s delay. If the case already uses .crt::before, draw it on an aria-hidden span.roll inside .crt-tube, above the scanlines.
- On Home, a white-hot head (#e4fff0 core, 14px bloom) runs along the sill from the NOW lamp to station one over .9s and lights the run behind it; the airglow fades up after it.
- Nothing loops. Under reduced motion, everything shows lit at once. The harness's motion-on frames at 60, 220, 450 and 900ms, clipped to the Next up tube, should catch the sweep.

E. THE LINEAGE'S KEY FIXES.
- 'Here' becomes T1-32: a #26313a latched cell with a 2px steel cap and a ring lamp, replacing the backlit slab in the bar, tabs, keys and on the month.
- The question 'What are we planning?' at 40px Archivo 700 condensed, with 'planning' in E1's two layers. Box E4, Send E3.
- Setup keeps its horizontal line. All stops are hollow amber rings; the current one has a phosphor rim and 'Next step' at 13px. Run-in bold actions. The rail ends at a T buffer beside 'All the setup steps'.
- Chat: 'Vera' flush left with the lede under it. Rails 18px apart, each time printed once on the spine. Only the newest stop lit. 'your turn' at the ring on the composer.
- Ideas' line from home: only the nearest, furthest and pointed-at stations named in words. The axis starts at 15 min behind one 45° jog. Every row lights its station, with :has() rules to 40 rows.
- Plans: the head reads '5 coming / next tomorrow 10:00'. The month's week rails are dropped: the ink plates now carry the plans. Today is the latched cell.
- Kind rings in terracotta #df987c (restaurant), moss #b5c87d (outing) and wheat #c3a85d (seasonal), with the kind words in ink-2.
- Row afterglow as a 2px sage edge with an 18px halo, on in .12s, off over 1.2s.
- Nothing under 13px, and 0 targets under 44px.
- Budget: the sheet is at 57.2K of 60K. Pay for this by deleting the shelf and its well, the Coming up tray, the backlit key and the week-rail rules, and keep geometry in SVG presentation attributes. Forms keep csrf and once tokens, with no inline style. Reduced motion, more contrast and forced colours are kept.

briefs.avoids: 'Home is still the parent's' (style, system, skeptic, soul): the greeting and Coming up become one lit board standing on its own line, with the tube as the first stop, so Home changes above the fold. 'Nearly all steel and green' (feedback, style, system, skeptic): the family's plates, bubbles and fields become an ink solid with a job. 'The shelf's lamps have no names and only repeat the list' (interaction, usability, skeptic): the lamps become named, counted strings on the glass that link to their boards, and the separate well with its dead slate is gone. 'The greeting's lit pool is lost' and 'the lit run is too small to see' (soul): the airglow rises off the lit run, and the run sets itself on opening. 'The week rail only reads under the last row' (system, skeptic, interaction): dropped. Also: the backlit slab, the colliding station numbers, the backwards chat title, 'Plans 1' over three plans, amber on Restaurant, and 'What's next for us?'. It does not import any main-line structure (no cased terminal column beside a desk, no listing bands with a head column, no cut plate, no big quote), and it leaves the pocket's vertical NOW spine, the timetable's line down from her screen and the console's arcs to their lineages.
briefs.title: What are we *planning*? This title is untried. It is the household's own present tense: it asks what the family has on the go and invites them to tell Vera, and on this Home the lit line of plans the question stands on answers it directly below. The lit word is the job, not the motif. It avoids 'next', which the tube's NEXT UP already claims beside it, and 'shall', which the judges found stiff. At 21 characters it holds one line at 28-32px on a phone, and as the box's label it tells a first-time user what the box is for.
